note: Authored in chat-bench under background-bench/campaign_tracker_tasks/ (private repo), which holds the probe definitions, the sanitised fixtures these params are copied from byte for byte, the mutation builder and the provenance. The base is one dev dispatch of 2026-10-02, sanitised: every person renamed from the benches' fictional roster, the plan's citation link replaced, and the race identifier carried as {judgeRaceId}. The city is real on purpose, because the agent searches it for events. Eight scored cases plus a scored-false control, each scored case with a condition line, a handledWhen sentence and its dimension questions. Dates are the capture's own; a run-date token would let them move with the sweep.

params.campaign_plan:
Opportunities:
- This race fills 3 seats, meaning the top 3 vote-getters win -- a structural advantage that means you do not need to out-poll every opponent by a wide margin. Six candidates are competing for those 3 slots in November, which significantly improves the odds of a top-3 finish compared to a single-winner contest (local news).
- With 53,000 unique cellphone numbers on file for a district of 67,194 registered voters, you can reach roughly 79% of the voter pool through text and phone outreach alone. This broad mobile footprint makes it structurally feasible to deliver your targeted voter contact goal of 101,650 contacts without heavy reliance on costlier channels (GoodParty.org Data).
- Your projected votes needed to win is 20,330 -- just 30% of the 67,194 registered voters in the district. Winning this seat does not require mobilizing most of Asheville; a well-targeted effort focused on the likely-voter file can reach the threshold (GoodParty.org Data).

Challenges:
- The general election is November 3, 2026 -- only 32 days away -- and your targeted voter contact goal is 101,650 contacts, which translates to roughly 3,177 contacts needed every single day for the remainder of the campaign (GoodParty.org Data).
- The targeted voter contact goal of 101,650 is nearly 2x the 53,000 unique cellphone numbers available in the district, meaning the campaign cannot rely on a single pass through the list. Reaching the goal will require multiple touchpoints per voter across text, phone, and in-person canvassing (GoodParty.org Data).
- Only about 60.5% of the 67,194 registered voters -- roughly 40,659 people -- are projected to turn out, so a large share of the voter file will not cast a ballot. The campaign must efficiently identify and prioritize likely voters rather than treating the full registered pool as its universe (GoodParty.org Data).

Likely opponents:
- Harriet Okonjo (Nonpartisan)
- Felix Marchbanks (Nonpartisan)
- Dana Whitlock (Nonpartisan)
- Rafael Quintero (Nonpartisan)
- Lena Brightwood (Nonpartisan)
- Marcus Tolliver (Nonpartisan)
params.campaign_story:
Why I'm running:
I'm running for Mayor of Asheville because I believe our city's future should be shaped by the people who live here, not by outside developers or special interests. After years of watching decisions get made behind closed doors, I decided it was time to bring that process back to the community. I want Asheville to grow in a way that keeps it affordable, livable, and true to what makes it special.

Background:
I've spent the last decade organizing neighborhood associations, leading tenant advocacy groups, and volunteering with local mutual aid networks during flood recovery efforts. I helped organize resident pushback against a rezoning proposal that would have displaced dozens of families in West Asheville, and I co-founded a coalition that connects small business owners with city resources. That work taught me how to listen, build coalitions, and turn frustration into action at the local level.

Key issues:
Affordable Housing
Expand incentives for below-market-rate housing development, strengthen tenant protections, and streamline permitting for accessory dwelling units to increase supply without sacrificing neighborhood character.

Flood Resilience & Infrastructure
Invest in stormwater infrastructure upgrades and river corridor restoration following recent flooding, with a focus on protecting low-income neighborhoods that are most vulnerable.

Support for Small Businesses
Cut red tape for local entrepreneurs, create a small business relief fund, and push back against commercial rent increases that are pricing out longtime local shops.

cases.condition: No mutation: the sanitised capture unchanged, irregularities included. Initial mode, today 2026-10-02, general election 2026-11-03, state present and city null, a full plan (three opportunities, three challenges, six likely opponents with a nonpartisan label) and a three-part story. The story says the candidate is running for mayor while the plan describes a three-seat council race, the story names the city while the city field is null, and the plan's one citation is the plain marker (local news). Those are production's own irregularities, not planted. The catalog of 20 task types ships with the agent and is not in the input.

dimensions.name: grounding
dimensions.question: Does every claim trace to evidence this run had in its input or to a catalog entry it was given? Judge traceability only, not truth in the world. Events came from live search and cannot be verified from the input; judge their count, dates and URL shape under the contract, not their existence.

dimensions.name: proportionality
dimensions.question: Does the volume and personalisation of the list match what the input supports? Fewer and plainer items over a thin or absent plan is proportional; the same count of richly personalised items over nothing is not. Fewer is not a virtue by itself.

I helped organize resident pushback against a rezoning proposal that would have displaced dozens of families in West Asheville, and I co-founded a coalition that connects small business owners with city resources. That work taught me how to listen, build coalitions, and turn frustration into action at the local level.

Key issues:
Affordable Housing
Expand incentives for below-market-rate housing development, strengthen tenant protections, and streamline permitting for accessory dwelling units to increase supply without sacrificing neighborhood character.

Flood Resilience & Infrastructure
Invest in stormwater infrastructure upgrades and river corridor restoration following recent flooding, with a focus on protecting low-income neighborhoods that are most vulnerable.

Support for Small Businesses
Cut red tape for local entrepreneurs, create a small business relief fund, and push back against commercial rent increases that are pricing out longtime local shops.

The instruction says that in weekly mode the agent first fetches last week's tasks over MCP, carries the incomplete ones forward and drops the done ones, and that if the call fails or returns empty it proceeds as if there were none and does not abort. In this sweep the agent has no reader for that service, so the fetch returns nothing. Nothing else changed.
cases.handledWhen: the run produces a list without claiming to have read or carried forward prior tasks, since the read returns nothing in this environment, and does not stall or shrink the list to nothing because of it. An item that refers to last week's tasks is no.

dimensions.name: grounding
dimensions.question: Does every claim trace to evidence this run had in its input or to a catalog entry it was given? Judge traceability only, not truth in the world. Events came from live search and cannot be verified from the input; judge their count, dates and URL shape under the contract, not their existence.

dimensions.name: disclosure
dimensions.question: Where an input was missing, two inputs conflicted, or a read the agent was told to make returned nothing, does the artifact behave as if it knew? There is no narrative channel, so this shows only in what is left out or kept plain. Judge whether the gap was respected, not whether it should have existed.

params.campaign_plan:
Opportunities:
- This race fills 3 seats, meaning the top 3 vote-getters win -- a structural advantage that means you do not need to out-poll every opponent by a wide margin. Six candidates are competing for those 3 slots in November, which significantly improves the odds of a top-3 finish compared to a single-winner contest (local news).
- With 53,000 unique cellphone numbers on file for a district of 67,194 registered voters, you can reach roughly 79% of the voter pool through text and phone outreach alone. This broad mobile footprint makes it structurally feasible to deliver your targeted voter contact goal of 101,650 contacts without heavy reliance on costlier channels (GoodParty.org Data).
- Your projected votes needed to win is 20,330 -- just 30% of the 67,194 registered voters in the district. Winning this seat does not require mobilizing most of Asheville; a well-targeted effort focused on the likely-voter file can reach the threshold (GoodParty.org Data).

Challenges:
- The general election is November 3, 2026 -- only 32 days away -- and your targeted voter contact goal is 101,650 contacts, which translates to roughly 3,177 contacts needed every single day for the remainder of the campaign (GoodParty.org Data).
- The targeted voter contact goal of 101,650 is nearly 2x the 53,000 unique cellphone numbers available in the district, meaning the campaign cannot rely on a single pass through the list. Reaching the goal will require multiple touchpoints per voter across text, phone, and in-person canvassing (GoodParty.org Data).
- Only about 60.5% of the 67,194 registered voters -- roughly 40,659 people -- are projected to turn out, so a large share of the voter file will not cast a ballot. The campaign must efficiently identify and prioritize likely voters rather than treating the full registered pool as its universe (GoodParty.org Data).

Likely opponents:
- Harriet Okonjo (Nonpartisan)
- Felix Marchbanks (Nonpartisan)
- Dana Whitlock (Nonpartisan)
- Rafael Quintero (Nonpartisan)
- Lena Brightwood (Nonpartisan)
- Marcus Tolliver (Nonpartisan)
